rows: Pro Forma Consolidated Revenue Run Rate
Record Q3: revenue $20.4M (+23% reported, +45% ex one-time items); return to positive net income of ~$1M ($0.02/share) vs $4.2M loss in Q3 2018.
North America grew 48% (66% normalized) on distribution expansion - DSD network 70+ partners, 60,000+ retail locations (+57% in 2019).
Convenience-channel SPINS growth of 41.1% (4.3x category) at only 11.9% ACV - long runway, basis for 2020 planogram resets.
Post-quarter acquisition of Nordic partner Func Food Group for ~$24.2M lifts pro forma revenue run rate to ~$100M and adds the FAST protein-bar business.
China royalty/license shift reduced Asia revenue but was margin-accretive - removed ~$5.1M of quarterly marketing spend.
Europe down 11% on timing of flavor launches/promotions/orders - since remediated; Nordic partner saw strong Peach Vibe and Frozen Berry demand.
Gross margin improved to 42.2%; adjusted EBITDA $2.4M vs -$2.9M prior year.
DSD conversion expected to drive ~40% sales lift in converted outlets; NYC flipped first (7-Eleven to Big Geyser, Target conversion in November).
DSD buildout roughly one-third complete - 250-300 distributors needed for national coverage, methodical mapped process through 2020.
Func Food was working-capital constrained from over-leverage; new capital relieves the pressure; division led by Robin Lybeck.
BCAA recovery line (debuted at Mr. Olympia) and FAST bar launches expected to add meaningful growth in 2020.
FAST protein-snack US launch will be methodical (online + fitness channel in 2020, some vitamin specialty), protecting EBITDA with Celsius as main focus.
Management highly optimistic about momentum into 2020 buyer-season planogram resets; Celsius a 'top pick' for buyers.
Discuss cash generation, whether the company expects to generate cash going forward, and confirm cash balance is post-acquisition.

Confirmed $20.5M cash is after the acquisition; ~$3.5M cash generated in Q3; expects to keep generating cash depending on working-capital needs. Escrow funds earmarked; large Oct-Dec production runs consume working capital ahead of strong Q1/Q2 demand.
Elaborate on new retailers being added (some may be tests) and what other retailers Celsius could enter.

Started retailer tests late 2018, announced Target/CVS in Q1, currently testing in undisclosed retailers/markets. Buyers in 2020 category-rationalization season; Celsius a 'top pick' given strong third-party data and on-trend better-for-you positioning.
Improvement in stock-outs, next key DSD network milestones, and timing of Target conversion to DSD.

High velocity creates stock-out problems under warehouse model; DSD conversion fixes it - ~40% lift expected in some outlets. Network grew from ~6 to 70+ partners; NYC flipped first (7-Eleven to Big Geyser, Target conversion in November), Arizona/Michigan/Southeast next.
How far along the DSD network is - a third, halfway, or otherwise.
About a third of the way; anticipates 250-300 distributors needed for national coverage, methodical mapped-out process for filling geographic gaps through 2020.
Expected quarterly cost to carry the $9.4M of Func debt and confirmation of closing date.
Deal closed October 25; quarterly interest carry ~$200K-$300K; good cash to service it; exploring long-term financing given otherwise clean, essentially debt-free balance sheet.
Timelines for the FAST protein-snack portfolio and when North America introductions happen and in what channels.

Opportunity in protein snack bar category but methodical, profit-focused approach - testing 2020 via online and fitness channel, some vitamin specialty retailers likely in 2020, while protecting EBITDA and keeping Celsius the main focus.
Trends or recent activity from online channels in Q3 and outlook for Q4.

Online activity strong - Google Analytics, walmart.com, amazon.com momentum; Amazon sales extremely strong over 3-4 years with high continuity. Plans to expand digital presence with retail partners and pursue shopping apps in 2020 as an untapped channel.
Func Foods revenue run rate & Q4 growth
Given Func's standalone ~$24-25M annual revenue, what is the current quarterly run rate and should it grow in Q4.

Confirmed Q4 growth - flawless Peach Vibe/Frozen Berry launches (sold out of initial runs), ~20% lift in Celsius portfolio last quarter. Q4 holiday season traditionally slower in Nordic retail; ~$25M conservative consolidated revenue increase with embedded upside, no formal forward guidance.
How to gauge international sales excluding the China model change, and whether the international opportunity is significant.

Asia was ~$2.7M last year; in 2019 ~$630K generated in Asia plus ~$160K other sales - growing on a backed-out basis. Significant opportunity with Func Food; ongoing Asia opportunities despite troubled Hong Kong retail; Malaysia launch seeding into 2,000+ 7-Elevens. Disciplined international growth, North America the main focus.
Whether any flavors might be discontinued in favor of better performers, and whether new marketing campaigns are planned.

Always reviews SKU rationalization - kiwi guava #1 per point; lower-velocity flavors like Cola retained as online channels and small co-packer runs meet hurdle rates. No discontinuations planned. 2020 marketing: experiential sampling (Live Fit Tour, Tough Mudder), social/digital influencer, trade marketing with 100-case stack displays via DSD.
What role management envisions for the HEAT sub-line, given it lines up with fitness-energy leader Bang.

HEAT faced tough Q2 competition (REIGN BOGO, Bang/VPX discounting) but seen as a major player in performance energy, drawing retailer interest, expected to be a major portfolio contributor. Expects 16-oz competitive set to stay very competitive into 2020.
